description:
Declare numeric stats on threads, log values, and show them as a series by day, week or month.

Subcommands:
  new NAME --thread THREAD --type TYPE --agg AGG — declare a stat in the thread file's frontmatter
  list [--json] — list declared stats
  log NAME VALUE [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] — buffer a value of a declared stat
  series NAME [--by PERIOD] [--since DATE] [--until DATE] [--json] — value per period from logs and the unflushed buffer

Flags:
  new:
    NAME  lowercase letters, digits and '-'; unique across the vault; include a unit if unclear (run-km, spend-zar)
    --thread THREAD  required; thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink
    --type  required; int (counts, steps, events) or decimal
    --agg  required; sum adds a period's values, last takes the latest, max the largest
  list:
    --json  JSON output
  log:
    NAME  from stats list
    VALUE  whole number for int; plain number such as 12.50 for decimal (no exponent)
    -d, --date YYYY-MM-DD  default today
    -t, --time HH:MM  default now
  series:
    --by  day, week or month; default day; weeks start Monday
    --since / --until YYYY-MM-DD
    --json  JSON output; empty periods are null (text shows '-'), not 0

Examples:
  ["new", "pushups", "--thread", "Topics/Fitness", "--type", "int", "--agg", "sum"]
  ["log", "pushups", "25"]
  ["log", "run-km", "5.2", "-d", "2026-10-06", "-t", "18:05"]
  ["series", "pushups", "--by", "week", "--json"]

Notes:
  For an event (yes/no), declare an int stat and log 1 each time: agg sum counts occurrences, agg max shows whether it happened.
  log writes to buffer.md; buffer flush files it as a STAT: line in threads/<Kind>/<Name>/logs/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md. series reads the buffer too.
  new edits the thread file in place. No rename or delete.
  Exit 1 (nothing written): name undeclared or declared twice; value of wrong type; bad -d/-t; new with a bad or taken name, unresolvable thread, or frontmatter it cannot safely edit; series hits a malformed logged value; --since after --until.
  Exit 2: usage error (missing argument, unknown --type or --agg).
